statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = n and for every x with 0 <= x < n the following holds. Let W_x be the set of all k >= 0 for which there exists an alternating walk from node 0 to node x of length k. If W_x is nonempty, then r[x] = min(W_x); if W_x is empty, then r[x] = -1. An alternating walk of length k is a sequence of nodes p_0, ..., p_k with p_0 = 0 and p_k = x together with colors c_0, ..., c_{k-1} in {red, blue} such that for each j with 0 <= j < k, c_j = red implies redEdges contains [p_j, p_{j+1}] and c_j = blue implies blueEdges contains [p_j, p_{j+1}], and for each j with 0 <= j < k-1, c_j != c_{j+1}. Here redEdges contains [a,b] means there is an index i with redEdges[i] = [a,b], and similarly for blueEdges. For k = 0 the sequence has no colors and the walk exists exactly when x = 0. Length means number of edges.
preconditions: n is an i64 with 1 <= n <= 100. The slices redEdges and blueEdges satisfy 0 <= len(redEdges) <= 400, 0 <= len(blueEdges) <= 400, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(redEdges), len(redEdges[i]) = 2, 0 <= redEdges[i][0] < n, and 0 <= redEdges[i][1] < n; for every j with 0 <= j < len(blueEdges), len(blueEdges[j]) = 2, 0 <= blueEdges[j][0] < n, and 0 <= blueEdges[j][1] < n. Edges are 0-indexed pairs [source, target]; self-edges and parallel edges are allowed.
